messages.author: 2f6c5eed34f4bc17
messages.subject: Details about INLA optimization
parts:
Hello,

I am interested in learning what actual optimization method(s) INLA uses under the hood for finding the conditional mode. I found this thread:

http://www.r-inla.org/?place=msg%2Fr-inla-discussion-group%2FIHS2DLn5jyw%2F6DCYXZEskKwJ

which appears to be cold. Is there any paper or documentation on how the underlying GMRFlib does its optimization? I saw something about "conjugate gradient" in the source code comments, and the original INLA paper essentially describes Newton's method. What is actually done?

Related, does INLA use any tricks for doing this optimization so many times? My understanding is that it needs to do it once per value of theta. Does it, for example, use the mode from the previous value of theta as the starting value for the optimization for a new value of theta, or something like this?

Any help is much appreciated!

Thanks,

Alex

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Details about INLA optimization
parts:
for the latent field, I'm afraid you have to read the code, like this
function

int GMRFLib_init_GMRF_approximation_store__intern(GMRFLib_problem_tp **
problem, double *x, double *b, double *c, double *mean,

in

approx-inference.c


it uses a (modified) trust region Newton method. In most cases the
trust region is not needed, as there exists a good initial values (the
previous found mode for the same thread).


for the hyperparmeter, it uses a modified bfgs algorithm, defined in
the file

bfgs3.c

where this code is modified from the GSL implementation (the file
vector_bfgs2.c I think, in the GSL library).


H
